Hi Asha / Lyra team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the clear framing on business impact. Short recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of pain & goals we captured
- Production inference latency and variance are causing customer complaints on your mobile app (target UX p95 ~ <150ms).
- Current hosted vendor is unreliable at peak and costs spike on burst; you want predictable unit economics.
- Goal: migrate top two models behind Lyra Assist (intent detection + response generation) to a platform that meets p95 latency SLA, reduces per-token cost by 25-40%, and supports gradual cutover.

Quantitative constraints you gave
- Peak QPS: ~300 inference requests/sec (US-west) with 99% of requests under 800 tokens; tails up to 2048 tokens for heavy docs.
- Target SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, cold-start p99 < 400ms for single-shot API.
- Budget guidance: comparable to current vendor; prefer predictable reserved capacity if material discount available.

Suggested technical approach (high level)
- Dedicated pools in us-west for steady traffic + autoscale policy for bursts to multi-zone hosted.
- Model variants: quantized 16-bit for latency-sensitive path; fallback to float32 variant for quality checks.
- KV/prefix caching for short-lived user contexts to reduce token compute.

\Attachments
- Attached a draft SLO matrix (lyra_slo_matrix.xlsx) and a sketch of recommended deployment zones/topology (redwood-deploy-topology.png).

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Marcus and Jonas to review topology and suggest any constraints we should consider for your infra (networking, egress, VPC peering).
2) Asha: confirm whether Lyra requires on-prem/VPC private deployment or if Dedicated hosted with customer-managed VPC is sufficient.
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive this week to map model sizes, exact token distributions, and traffic shaping rules.

Proposed times: Thurs 4/8 10am PT or Fri 4/9 9am PT — let me know what works.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik / team — quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow's deep-dive so we target the right data points: 

1) Model sizing & variants to surface during call
- Candidate model: open LLM family (we discussed Llama-2 style 70B variant) — bring both a quantized int8/llm-q8 variant and a full fp16 build for quality head-to-head.
- If Lyra's accuracy delta on quantized model is acceptable (~<1.5% top-level metric), we can default traffic to quantized.

2) Latency/throughput baseline assumptions (for design)
- Single GPU p95 token latency targets: ~25-35ms per 1k tokens (batching/caching dependent). For Lyra's token mix (median ~120 tokens), expect p95 per-request compute ~30-45ms on A100/RTX 6000 class with optimized kernels.
- End-to-end p95 budget: compute + network + routing + KV cache miss. We should plan compute budget ~60-80ms, network + routing 20-40ms depending on VPC peering.
- For 300 QPS steady with ~120 token median, target pool: 6-8 GPUs with concurrent batching and autoscale headroom. We will validate with a perf test.

3) Deployment topology options to discuss
- Option A (Dedicated Primary): Dedicated us-west pool behind Redundant Load Balancer + cross-zone fallback. Best for predictability and cost.
- Option B (Hybrid): Dedicated steady-state + hosted burst in multi-zone to absorb flash traffic. Lower committed footprint, slightly higher tail variance.
- Option C (Private/VPC): Customer-managed VPC with private control plane — required if Lyra moves PII. Higher ops and lead time.

4) Observability & regressions
- We'll instrument per-model token-level tracing, per-route p50/p95/p99, and deploy a small prompt-monitoring eval to detect quality regressions on quantized variants.

Attachments: I'll upload a brief test plan and a draft perf-run script (link in call notes).

I'll join the Fri 9am PT call; will prepare a small perf simulation.
